intent: Changed: wheel_track from 0.12 to 0.10 m, to raise turn rate per unit of wheel differential as the Integrator advised once line loss returned near 0.1. Kept: five sensors at x = -0.06 to +0.06 in 0.03 m steps, y 0.03, 16 mm footprints, mass 0.8, body_length 0.18, body_width 0.12, wheel_radius 0.03. Expected result: max_error falls from about 0.063 m toward or below 0.06 m on slalom and s-bend, off_track ends fall, and line loss stays near 0.1 or below. Considering, not committed: mass 0.7 with body_length 0.18 if slalom line loss rises to 0.2 or more with the narrower track, and wheel_radius changes if progress is too low on the oval.
learning: Iteration 5 confirmed that inertia (mass and body_length) drives slalom line loss, while sensor y and span are settled. The open question is whether turn authority alone can bring max_error under 0.06 m. This race tests that on the current platform. If max_error stays at about 0.063 m even with wheel_track 0.10, the limit is probably the controller's gain balance rather than geometry, and I will say so in the next feedback request.
rationale: Iteration 5 reverted mass to 0.8 and body_length to 0.18 with sensor y 0.03 and the 0.06 m span. It scored 111.80, matching iteration 1. Slalom line loss fell from 0.85 to 0.10, which confirms that the reduced inertia from iteration 4 caused the slalom line loss. The cost was the s-bend and oval progress gain from lower inertia. The Integrator's rule for this case is to hold the geometry and, if line loss is near 0.1 while max_error stays near 0.063 m, to test wheel_track 0.10. Both conditions hold: slalom line loss is 0.10, and max_error on slalom is 0.0636 m, still above the 0.06 m off-track limit. I am taking that advice. Turn rate per unit of wheel differential scales with 1/wheel_track, so narrowing the track from 0.12 to 0.10 m gives about 20 percent more turn authority at the same controller output. I keep the sensors (five at x = -0.06 to +0.06, y 0.03, 16 mm), mass 0.8, body_length 0.18, body_width 0.12 and wheel_radius 0.03 unchanged, so this race isolates the track change. The expected result is max_error below 0.06 m on more trials, with line loss staying near 0.1. The risk is that higher turn authority increases steering oscillation on the slalom, which I will watch. The mass 0.7 alternative from the Integrator stays in reserve. I am not adding sensors, because line loss is controllable at this span.
